content.identity:
**Paolo Ricci** is verified as the Full Professor and **Director of the SPC - Theory group** at EPFL, with current office at PPB 318, EPFL SB SPC-TH, Station 13, 1015 Lausanne, Switzerland. EPFL's people directory confirms his email paolo.ricci@epfl.ch and tags him Director of four SPC sub-units (Theory; Low Temperature Plasma Physics and Applications; International Installations; TCV Tokamak Physics; Material Group), as well as Full Professor within EDPY (Enseignement de la Physique) and SPH (School of Physics) teaching units [identity[0]] [7].

He was previously the holder of the SPC Chair of Theory and succeeded Ambrogio Fasoli as Director of the Swiss Plasma Center on June 1, 2024 [identity[1]] [14]. The EPFL SPC Annual Report 2024 corroborates this: under the "A word from the Directors" section, Ambrogio Fasoli writes "After a few months of overlap, Prof. Paolo Ricci, became the new Director of the Center, in July 2024," and the report's organization chart lists Ricci as head of both "Finance" and "Theory" [identity[2]] [50]. The slight discrepancy in transition date (June 1 vs. July) is noted but not material; both sources confirm the 2024 hand-over.

Research focus: development of numerical codes for fusion-plasma simulation, scrape-off layer turbulence, plasma-wall interactions, kinetic-fluid modeling using codes such as GBS, ORB5, VENUS-LEVIS, and VENUS-KMHD, plus high-performance/supercomputing on CSCS, CINECA, and the EPFL EUROfusion Advanced Computing Hub [identity[2]] [50].

**Namesaker exclusion**: A "Paolo Ricci" at the Latin American Centre, Oxford (paolo-ricci@lac.ox.ac.uk) is a professor of Political Science at the University of Sao Paulo - a different individual - and should not be conflated [identity[3]] [10]. Likewise, LinkedIn returns a "paolo ricci - Professor at University of Bologna" whom we treat as distinct from paolo.ricci@epfl.ch [identity[4]] [36]. Our subject is confirmed by the email paolo.ricci@epfl.ch and the EPFL/SPC unit codes (SPC-TH/SPC).

  - The SNSF data portal result row itself is canonical, but the row text in the portal renders grant attributes without a canonical grant-id URL; citation points to the search URL rather than a /show/<id> deep link because no such ID renders for this row in the available extract.
  - We did not find a public LinkedIn post by Paolo Ricci announcing recent funding or hiring. Public LinkedIn posts may exist but were not surfaced by the search runs in this session; absence reflects search limitations, not a definitive "no".
  - The closed-position side of the hiring scope for 2026-01-01-onwards is empty in this research run - explicitly marked as "No verified public evidence found." This is not the same as "no such postings exist".
  - EUROfusion funding flows to SPC as a consortium member; we cannot, on the basis of public sources, attribute a personal competitive grant to Ricci for 2024+ in that channel. This is consistent with the EPFL profile's bibliographic note being silent on any 2024+ competitive award to him personally.
  - The SNSF search returned 7 results; one ("GROUND TESTS") is unrelated to P. Ricci at EPFL (Jamie Allen + Donato Ricci at FHNW). It is excluded from the lead funding table.
content.synthesis:
Comparing the three sub-source types (SNSF data portal, EPFL SPC site, LinkedIn) on the same dimensions:

- **Mechanism of verification**: SNSF data portal is the only quantitative arbiter (CHF amounts, dates, status) for his SNSF grants; the EPFL people directory is the canonical identity/role arbiter; LinkedIn is corroboration-only and lags in grants/hiring detail.
- **Scope of evidence per channel**: SNSF = 1 active + 1 just-closed + 5 historical project grants (Ricci PI or co-PI); EPFL = profile + 1 active year-round PhD under his name + 1 open postdoc (under Coda, not Ricci) + 12.5M CHF institutional envelope; LinkedIn = profile and endorsement metadata only.
- **Trade-offs**: the SNSF CHF 810'378 active grant is a competitive personal PI grant, but is scoped to plasma detachment (a continuous overlap with the core Theory-physics work). The institutional and consortium envelopes (Swiss Fusion Hub, EUROfusion TSVV-2, EUROfusion Advanced Computing Hub) are mission/consortium funding, not competitive grants to Ricci. We do not claim them as personal funding. The single open Ricci-led position is the PhD year-round; secondary postdoc hires are SPC-wide, channeled by other group members.
- **Forward-looking note (heads-up)**: SNSF "Laufend" status for the 4-year grant (through 31.03.2028) likely supports doctoral/postdoctoral effort on plasma detachment topics. Any recruitment directly under that grant is plausible to surface on the SPC PhD-posting page (which already lists a tokamak-edge simulation project under Ricci), but the public sources do not explicitly link staff funding to a specific SNSF project, so per the task constraint we do NOT claim "funds available for a PhD" beyond what the EPFL SPC site explicitly states.
- **Divergence observed**: The EUROfusion news piece names June 1, 2024 as the transition date; the SPC Annual Report 2024 (written by Fasoli from the departing-director perspective) writes "in July 2024." Both are 2024 within one month and both primary; the slight discrepancy is preserved rather than smoothed over in this report.
